hook.text: Flat shapes were just the start — DNA origami now builds boxes, barrels, and wireframe polyhedra in 3D.

buildup.text: Multiple layers of DNA helices stack into solid 3D blocks — Shih's group built a solid 3D box in 2009.

discovery.text: Wireframe designs use less DNA — vertices and edges create hollow structures like an icosahedron with just staples.

twist.text: 3D structures are harder to fold correctly — misfolding and aggregation increase with structural complexity.

climax.text: A DNA box with a programmable lid was built — it opens only when specific molecular keys are present.

punchline.text: DNA folds into 3D containers — with locks only molecules can open.

quiz.question: What advance did wireframe DNA origami bring over solid block designs?
options: Wireframe structures are more colorful under microscopy
They use less DNA material to create hollow 3D shapes with maintained structural integrity
Wireframe designs fold faster because they use more staple strands
